chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There was in the pendant strap of the sword of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله a small parchment. So I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, "What was in that parchment?" He said, "They are the letters, each letter opening a thousand letters."
Abū Baṣīr said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said, "Then not even two letters from it will have come forth until the Hour."

key_terms.السَّاعَةِ: the Hour, meaning the final Hour or Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْأَحْرُفُ: letters, referring here to units or elements of knowledge
key_terms.ذُؤَابَةِ: the hanging strap or pendant part attached to the sword
key_terms.صَحِيفَةٌ: a small written parchment or sheet
key_terms.يَفْتَحُ: opens or unfolds into further meanings or knowledge

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about the parchment in the sword of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله say about hidden knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a small parchment associated with the sword of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله containing profound letters of knowledge, where each letter opens onto a thousand more. It emphasizes the vast, layered nature of divinely inherited knowledge and indicates that only a very small portion of it has appeared before the coming of the Hour.
